rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: ❌ Anode rays are a universal particle like cathode rays. ✅ Their e/m depends on the gas — they are positive ions of that gas; only the hydrogen ion (proton) is universal.  ·  ❌ Goldstein named and identified the proton fully. ✅ He discovered the rays; the proton was characterised later and named by Rutherford.

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: Statement 1: Definition of The Proton — Discovery & Properties of Anode Rays  ·  Statement 2: Theorem related to The Proton — Discovery & Properties of Anode Rays

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: **Problem:** Why do anode rays bend less than cathode rays in the same field? **Solution:** deflection ∝ q/m; the proton's q/m is ≈1836 times smaller than the electron's, so its curvature is correspondingly tiny.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: ❌ The proton is 1837 times heavier than the electron. ✅ 1836 (the neutron is 1839).

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ### Focus of this tab  ·  How the proton was found: Goldstein's anode (canal) rays, the mass spectrometry evidence, and Rutherford's 1919 transmutation — the second particle needed to build the nuclear atom.

rows.label: Study notes
rows.text: ### Anode (canal) rays, 1886  ·  Goldstein used a perforated (perforated-cathode) discharge tube: besides cathode rays, a new radiation passed *through* the holes of the cathode in the direction opposite to cathode rays. Properties: travel in straight lines, deflected by E and B fields in the direction of *positive* charges, and the e/m value **depends on the gas** in the tube — so these are positive ions of…  ·  ### The lightest positive particle

rows.text: Write Rutherford's nitrogen transmutation equation and state its two conclusions.  ·  Give the charge, mass and e/m of the proton.  ·  Rutherford's transmutation opened nuclear chemistry: element synthesis beyond bismuth became possible.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: With hydrogen in the tube the e/m is the largest observed (9.58 × 10⁷ C kg⁻¹), i.e. the lightest positive particle: the proton, with charge +1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C and mass 1.673 × 10⁻²⁷ kg = 1.00728 u ≈ 1836 electron masses. The proton is the nuclear constituent that carries the atomic number Z.  ·  ### Rutherford's transmutation (1919)  ·  Bombarding nitrogen with α-particles produced protons and oxygen: $^{14}\text{N}+\,^{4}\text{He}\rightarrow\,^{17}\text{O}+\,^{1}\text{p}$. This was the first artificial nuclear reaction: it (i) proved protons exist inside nuclei, (ii) changed one element into another (contra Dalton), and (iii) named the particle…

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: ### Why the proton matters for structure  ·  The nuclear charge Z counted in protons is the element's identity (Moseley); A = Z + N requires neutrons as well, since protons alone cannot account for the masses and stability of nuclei (electrostatic repulsion of like charges would fly apart — the strong interaction and neutrons are needed).
